item.title: Drivers in Gallia and Meigs counties among the least distracted, according to new study
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio — A newly released study finds that Ohio drivers are less distracted behind the wheel compared with the nationwide average.

item.title: The French Art Colony continues long legacy of cultural enrichment in Gallia County
item.description: GALLIPOLIS, Ohio — The French Art Colony, a regional multi-arts center in Gallipolis, continues its 62-year mission of enhancing the community’s quality of life through the arts, according to Executive Director Cynthia Sexton.

item.title: Mason County BOE hears updates and votes on personnel measures
item.description: POINT PLEASANT, W.Va. — The Mason County Board of Education approved a series of personnel transitions and student opportunities during its latest meeting, including a slate of new teaching hires and the authorization of a high-profile athletic trip.

item.title: Gallia County reports record economic development results in 2025
item.description: RIO GRANDE, Ohio — Gallia County Economic Development has announced record-setting results for development activity in 2025, with companies committing to create dozens of new jobs, invest millions of dollars and advance major initiatives expected to drive future growth.

item.title: Ohio opens new round of New Markets Tax Credit applications
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Applications are now open for the latest round of the Ohio New Markets Tax Credit Program, which aims to spur economic investment in underserved communities across the state, the Ohio Department of Development announced.

item.title: Haas Foundation donates $1 million to Marshall Advanced Manufacturing Center
item.description: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. — A new headquarters for the Marshall Advanced Manufacturing Center is one step closer to reality following a $1 million donation from the Gene Haas Foundation.

item.title: Mason mayor urges public support to keep senior nutrition program open
item.description: MASON, W.Va. — Mason Mayor Kristopher Clark is urging residents to speak out in an effort to keep the nutrition program operating at the Mason Senior Building.
